utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Judge Argibay won't be able to be with us because of other obligations. The remaining Judges have decided to continue the proceedings in accordance with Rule 15(B). Good morning, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can hear you, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please stand up. Would you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper the usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness answered through interpreter].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Ms. Issa, your witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning. Examined by Ms. Issa:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In a moment, sir, I'm going to be asking Madam Usher to be handing you a piece of paper with your name on it. And I'm going to be asking you whether or not that's your name without saying it out loud.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And for the record, Your Honour, that's Exhibit 721.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Just to start off, sir, with some information about your background. I understand that you are -- your ethnicity is that the of a Bosnian Serb. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Judges about your educational background.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I went to the wood processing industry school for three years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And when did you do that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at some point did you join the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: In 1989, I joined the Yugoslav People's Army -- I'm sorry, in 1988 that was, the end of 1988.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And were you with the army throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during the course of the war, sir, were you at some point a member of the Bosnian Serb Army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges when you joined the Bosnian Serb Army.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I don't remember whether it was March or April 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what unit did you join in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: The military police of Bihac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And how long did you work with the military police of Bihac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Several months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that, did you move to another unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes. The 2nd Battalion of the military police Drvar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And at some point did you receive any special training while you were in the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: No special training. I was at Mount Jahorina for training for several months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what kind of training did you receive at Mount Jahorina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Well, some sort of training for escorting people and providing security.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And providing security for what type of people in the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Persons and property.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Was there a particular rank of the army or members of the army that you were trained to provide security for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Who were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Brigade commanders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And at some point, sir, did you provide security for brigade commanders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: From 1993 to 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Where did you provide security in 1993, or to whom? What unit were you part of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Han Pijesak, Colonel Lazic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And after that did you move to another unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: The Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did that occur? When did you move to the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who did you provide security for in the Bratunac Brigade in 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Lieutenant Colonel Ognjenovic and Colonel Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And how long did you provide security for Lieutenant Ognjenovic before you provided for Colonel Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: A couple of months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what was the role of Lieutenant Colonel Ognjenovic and subsequently Colonel Blagojevic in the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Commander of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So can you describe your tasks as providing security for the commander of the Bratunac Brigade in 1995 for Commander Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Physical security.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Was there anybody else in 1995 who carried out these duties, aside from yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Goran Bojic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which one of you acted in that capacity most of the time? Was it yourself or Goran Bojic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Well, it was more me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Turning then to July of 1995, can you tell the Judges where you were on the day that Srebrenica fell.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I was at the Pribicevac hill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did you get there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: We arrived two or three days prior to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. When you say "we arrived," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Colonel Blagojevic, myself, and the driver.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And who was the driver?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Savo Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what were you doing there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Well, nothing. We were just present there, the command of the 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 3rd Battalion of which brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: The Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And how did you get to Pribicevac? What was your mode of transportation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: It was a Lada Niva vehicle, heavy duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And where did you pick up Colonel Blagojevic from before escorting him there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: The command of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Did you say it was at the command of the brigade that you picked him up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes, command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what route did you take to get there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Bratunac, Bjelovac, Rudnik, Sase, Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the day that Srebrenica fell whilst you were in Pribicevac, did Colonel Blagojevic give you any instructions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes. I went to a hill to inform some people about something, I think concerning food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, do you recall what he told you to inform them of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Well, I'm not quite sure, but it was something about food, to do with food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who were you going to inform or who did you inform? Who were these people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember. Actually, the people were from the Bratunac Brigade, but I don't know which people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And where was this hill?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Between Pribicevac at Zalazje. I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you get there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: On foot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far is this hill from Pribicevac, where the battalion is based?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. Maybe 1 or 2 kilometres thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And around what time of the day did this occur?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: About 10.00 or 11.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after you followed these instructions and informed them of whatever it is you informed them regarding the food, what did you do next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I stayed on that hill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For how long did you stay --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: At Zalazje. Four or five hours, roughly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you wait for four or five hours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Well, I waited for Colonel Blagojevic to return.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you expect him to return?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Because Colonel Blagojevic told me to wait for him and that he would return.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And did he return?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did you do after waiting for four or five hours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I took a truck and left towards the brigade, the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And just to clarify, where did you get the truck from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I think the truck happened to be passing by, or rather, it was there and he was going that way so I went with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And then when you went to the Bratunac Brigade, did you see Colonel Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you speak to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: No, I didn't, not then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you at some point find out that Srebrenica had fallen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall when that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: It was sometime in the afternoon, about 5.00 or 6.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it before or after you returned to the brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: When I returned to the brigade, that's when it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you said you returned to the Bratunac Brigade and saw Colonel Blagojevic there, did you see him leave the brigade at some point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Around what time did you see him at the brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: About 5.00 or 6.00, when I returned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was he doing there, from what you could see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I don't know. He was in his office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how long he stayed in his office?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Well, I think until he left to have a rest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know approximately what time that was that he left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: About 10.00 or 11.00 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Well, I think that's what it was, around about 10.00 or 11.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But what makes you think that he left around that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Well, I think I was at the porter's lodge when Colonel Blagojevic came out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where Colonel Blagojevic spent the night that evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I think in his flat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And do you know where his flat is in relation to the command or headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Some 200 metres away perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what makes you think that he spent the evening in his flat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Well, he left for his flat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, just as a point of clarification, sir, initially in your statement when you met with investigators on the 20th of February, you mentioned that you went to Pribicevac on the day that Srebrenica fell. You recall telling them that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes, yes. But I put that right later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And when did you do that? When did you put it right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Well, I corrected it straight away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when was the next time that you received instructions from Colonel Blagojevic after that day that you told us about, the day that Srebrenica fell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I think that was the following day when I went on leave to have a rest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what did -- what were the instructions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I think Colonel Blagojevic told me to stop by at the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what school was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Vuk Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And why -- did he tell you why he wanted you to stop by the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: To see that everything was all right there and to inform the policemen who were there, to tell them that there shouldn't be any problems.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And when you say "to see that everything was all right there," in relation to what? All right with what or with whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Well, I think that there was some people in the hall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I think there were people from Srebrenica who were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what makes you think that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Well, I think that the people were escorted there. They waited for the buses to go to the exchange, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what did Colonel Blagojevic tell you about the people that were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is that he wanted you to do in relation to those people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Just to inform the policemen so that they shouldn't make any problems vis-a-vis those people, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say "that they shouldn't make any problems," what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Not to allow somebody to come in there and make some problems towards those people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But I'd like you to tell us what you mean by "problems." If you can describe that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Well, probably that the policemen shouldn't allow anybody to enter and mistreat the people and provoke them or things of that kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did he tell you anything else when you gave you that instruction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Just to go and have a rest and that we would see each other the next morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did he tell you what you should do if you discovered that, in fact, people were being mistreated and there were problems?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: If there were any problems, he said I should inform him that same evening; if not, I could go and rest up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, before we get to what you did after having received these instructions, did you see any officers at the brigade that evening before you left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Well, there were some officers there, but I don't know who they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where they came from or what units they were connected to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a particular person that you recall seeing there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember. I think Major Pajic was just there. I saw Major Pajic from the brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was Major Pajic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I think he was head of the staff command of the brigade there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just to clarify, when you say "of the brigade," you're referring to the Bratunac Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, aside from Major Pajic, you said that there were other officers there. Do you recall their rank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Well, there was a lieutenant colonel, a colonel, there was a few generals. I really don't know who they all were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, aside from Pajic, whom you recall seeing from the Bratunac Brigade, did you see any other officers from the Bratunac Brigade that evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I think Nikolic was there, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And who was Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: He was in charge of security.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you see --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Performed security duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Sorry. What did you see him doing there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: He was present there in the brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him speaking to anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I think that Colonel Blagojevic just told him to make sure everything is as it should be, that's all. It was nothing else, so that everything is all right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Everything -- when he told him everything -- to make sure that everything should be -- everything's as it should be, sorry, or to make it right, what was he referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I don't know what he was referring to. He just told him to make sure that everything is all right, that there should be no problems, but I don't know what he meant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No problems towards whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not sure towards whom. He was entrusted with making sure that there were no problems, and this included the people who were at the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, getting back to that same day when you told us Colonel Blagojevic instructed you to check on the prisoners in Vuk Karadzic school, can you please tell the Judges what you did after receiving these instructions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I went to the school. I saw that there were police officers there. I spoke with them. I asked them if everything was all right. They said it was. And I conveyed to them Colonel Blagojevic's orders. They said that everything was all right, and then I went home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And when you say you saw there were police officers there, what unit were they connected to? Where were they from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: They were members of the Bratunac military police. There were also some civilian policemen, but I'm not sure where they were from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And how did you know that some of the officers were members of the Bratunac Brigade military police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I saw them before at the brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So you said that you went there, you spoke to these officers, and you told them what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I told them that Colonel Blagojevic said that there should be no problems, nothing else. I asked them whether everything was all right, and they said that it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And where were the prisoners located in the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: They were in the gym right behind the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you go inside the school to check on them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I didn't enter the gym.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how much time did you spend at the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I'm not sure. Maybe from 15 minutes to half an hour, maybe a little less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether the prisoners were ever removed from the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: They were taken away later, but I don't know where, where to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you report back to Colonel Blagojevic that evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Because everything was all right that evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Turning then to Exhibit 681.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can ask the assistance of Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I understand, sir, that when you and I met yesterday, you looked at this exhibit and you marked a couple of locations on it. Do you recall doing that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Issa, is that the correct number for that photo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I can check that, Your Honour. Perhaps you are right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm told it is, Your Honour. It's Exhibit 681. Perhaps there may have been a change at some point, and I apologise for any confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the document at my hands is in those documents, receipts, from Hotel Fontana, some bills, some coffee bills there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. I do believe that the updated list was provided to Your Honours this morning. Unfortunately we -- I only met with the witness late yesterday, so we didn't have an opportunity to divulge that information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed. I'll try to figure it out.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: We can certainly get Your Honour another copy at some point.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I was just indicating we can certainly get Your Honour another copy at some point during the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, you may proceed. We got it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, when you and I met yesterday you marked this exhibit. Is that correct? You marked a couple of locations on the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's a little bit hard to see, but what I'm going to ask you to do is to take the pointer that's sitting in front of you and to point firstly to the first location that you marked, which is marked with a triangle on the upper portion of the aerial. You have to do that on the ELMO, which is next to you, not on the screen, sir, because we won't be able to see it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So first you're pointing to the middle of the aerial where there's an X. Is that correct? You just pointed to that?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear whether the witness said yes or no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you repeat your last answer, sir, as the interpreter didn't hear it. Let me ask you again --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: This is the Vuk Karadzic school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you -- and for the record you just pointed to the middle of the picture that's marked X. That's the Vuk Karadzic school. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I see that on the upper corner right underneath the writing you have a triangle; it's very small. Perhaps to assist us, if you could please point to that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And can you tell us what that location is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: This is Colonel Blagojevic's apartment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And can you point to the command, if you can see it on the map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's a little bit off the map, but in that area.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you're pointing roughly around the letter S in the word Bosnia on the very top of the map, for the record.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Turning then to the next exhibit, Exhibit 720. All right. Now, this is a diagram that you drew in my office yesterday, is that correct, or a sketch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain what we are looking at here. I see that you have the letter S in one portion of the diagram. What does that refer to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: The school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And can you tell us where the gym is in relation to the school where you -- where the prisoners were located.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's the letter D. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I see at the very -- in between the school and the gym, you have two lines and it's marked P. What does that refer to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: It's the entrance to the school, next to the gym.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And can you explain whether the gym is attached or detached from the school.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Next to the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But is it a building that's attached to it or detached from it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Attached.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm finished with that exhibit, Madam Usher. Thank you for your help.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the following day after you -- you went to the school and then you told us you subsequently went home. Did you report back to the command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: The next morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Around what time was this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Before 7.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you see Colonel Blagojevic that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes. I saw him arriving at the brigade from his apartment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And around what time was this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Around 7.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you speak to him that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Just in passing very briefly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you at any point have an actual meeting with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: No. We just saw each other. He asked me what the situation was last night, was everything all right. I said that it was, and he said, "Very well."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did he do for the rest of the day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: He was there at the staff command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he leave the command at any point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I think that that day we just went to the rear base and then we returned immediately to the brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And where was -- where is the rear base located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: It's about 300 metres from the brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Not long. Maybe about 15 minutes, 10, 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you do there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I don't know. Colonel Blagojevic went inside. I was in front.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And can you explain to us what is the rear base.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: It's the base where food and clothing are stored, shoes and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Supplies is what you're saying -- telling us. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after you returned to the brigade headquarters, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I was there at the entrance, at the reception desk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was Colonel Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: He was in his office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see him or speak to him in the afternoon, after you returned from the base?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I cannot remember, but I think that we didn't see each other that day, not until the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And where did you see him in the evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: He left to go and rest at his apartment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And around what time was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you see any officers -- high-ranking officers from outside the Bratunac Brigade that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you do after Colonel Blagojevic left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I went to my wife's uncle's house, where I spent the night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that day, that same day that we were dealing with, do you know where were the prisoners that you saw the previous day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how long they remained in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what ultimately happened to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever discuss with Colonel Blagojevic what was the fate of the prisoners at the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Moving on then to the following day. What did you do the next day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I think that the next day we went to Milici. Yes, we went to Milici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Are you certain about that date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I cannot remember the dates now, but more or less I know that after that we went to Milici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what did you do in Milici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: The colonel went to the Milici Brigade, where he stayed for a while, and then we returned to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did he do at the Milici Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see where he went when he went to the -- when he was at the Milici Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: To the brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And when you say "he stayed for a while," how long was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I'm not sure. Maybe about half an hour to an hour, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. In relation to the day -- to the day that Srebrenica fell, how long after did this occur, that you went to Milici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Maybe some four or five days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. After you left Milici, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: We went to the brigade, the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you see anybody on your way along the -- on your way back to the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: There were soldiers from the Bratunac Brigade standing along the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where along the road were they standing? What road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: The Bratunac/Konjevic Polje road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were they doing there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: They were standing on the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did either you or Colonel Blagojevic speak to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: We stopped there for a little bit. The colonel went out, asked them if there were any problems, they said that there were none, and he said that if they should run into any prisoners they should bring them back to the brigade so that they would not be mistreated or provoked or anything like that, that they should treat them professionally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And aside from these soldiers, did you see anyone else on the road on the way back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I think that we met a man who was crossing the road. We stopped there. I went out. Colonel Blagojevic also went out. We asked him who he was. He didn't say anything. He was wounded. Then a truck came along. The colonel stopped the truck and told the driver to take him to the hospital, to urgently take him to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe this man.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: He had a camouflage jacket and military boots.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And do you know whether he was Muslim or Serb?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you initially went to Milici from Bratunac, what route did you take?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Bratunac, Konjevic Polje, Milici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what route did you return through? How did you return? What route did you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: The same route. We returned on the same route from Milici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we have a map sitting in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps if we can get the assistance of Madam Usher. Your Honour, that's Exhibit 680.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I understand, sir, while we're having the map moved, that you actually marked this map yesterday. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you put your initials and your signature at the bottom somewhere. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, I don't know if Your Honour can see the map or if it's come up on your screen. It hasn't come up on my mine yet. Perhaps we can wait a few -- a couple of moments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we have it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But not very clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Unfortunately I don't -- I have it now.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm sorry. You're right, Your Honour. It's getting clearer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, it's better.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you -- you drew a blue line on that map, sir, that's sitting in front of you. Can you take that pointer and point to the route you took from Bratunac to Milici and show us what you -- what route you took.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So that was from Bratunac, through Konjevic Polje, to Milici. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now aside from this trip, did you take any other trips after you went to Milici, after this trip with Colonel Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: We went to the bauxite mine one day and we stayed a little bit longer on one of those roads. And then afterwards, we returned to the brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And can you, while you have the map next to you there, show us the route that you took to go to the bauxite mines.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us what that route is, what roads you took.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I didn't understand. How do you mean, what is the road like?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, can you tell us what route you took, describe it in words.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Bratunac, Konjevic Polje, Milici, the bauxite mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And how did you return to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether we returned on the same route or whether we took the road via Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And who was the driver on this trip? Who was driving you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I think it was Milan Nedeljkovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how much time did you spend there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: We were there for about a couple of hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did Colonel Blagojevic do there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: There were soldiers from the Bratunac Brigade there, so we stopped by a little bit to be with them. And then we came back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did Colonel Blagojevic speak to the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: They talked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in the previous trip you told us about when you went to Milici, who was the driver on that trip? Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether it was Savo, or whether it was Pero.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall the last name of Savo or Pero?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: The two of them, Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, after the trip that you took to the bauxite mines, did you go on any other trips with Colonel Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Well, after several days we went to Drvar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And where is Drvar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: The Banja Lucka Krajina area, over there, towards Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how much time did you spend there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Perhaps two or three days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why did you go there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Well, the army -- the soldiers from the Bratunac Brigade were there, and Colonel Blagojevic went to visit the troops.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what route did you take to get to Drvar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: We took the Bratunac/Konjevic Polje/Vlasenica route, and we got into a car there. The Bratunac Brigade didn't have any available vehicles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you say you got into a car there, where are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: In Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what did you do with the vehicle that you were driving to Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: It remained there at the headquarters, whether it was the corps command or whatever, anyway, there, Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And after you attended at -- after Colonel Blagojevic checked on the troops in Drvar, where did go next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: We returned to the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what route did you take to return to the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Drvar, Kljuc, Mrkonjic Grad, Banja Luka, Bijeljina, Zvornik, Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall who was driving when you went to Drvar and returned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Milan Nedeljkovic was driving.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, aside from these places that you've told us about, did Colonel Blagojevic go anywhere else during the week following the fall of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I can't remember now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, yesterday when you and I met, I read out to you a daily combat report, which was dated the 16th of July, from the command of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may object. I don't see anything in the proofing notes where they use any material to refresh the witness's testimony. And I've repeatedly objected to this concept of trying to taint the witness's memories with previous documents they have. We don't have tape-recordings; now I hear for the first time that they're using documents to show to the witness. If at least they're going to give us a proofing note, which I got this morning, not yesterday, they should at least have the courtesy of telling us exactly what they're going to be putting on to it. And I'm very disturbed that they're using documents with witnesses prior to them taking their testimony because it taints their memory. It's not independent. They could do that here in court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, could you give us an explanation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I simply read out a portion of where -- of the report indicating where Colonel Blagojevic went and asked the witness whether he's aware of those locations. I don't think that taints the memory of the witness. I think it's something he can simply answer, indicating what he knows about them. I did not read out the entire report; I simply read out the portion that I was about to read -- refer to at this point, the locations specifically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think your objection is correctly registered in the transcript. We'll allow the Prosecution to proceed, and later on we'll assess this piece of the document and the evidence in the future.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I just want to -- I would just like a cautionary instruction to the Prosecution. They could do that here in court. I don't object to them showing him all sorts of documents, but I'm suspicious by nature. I can't help that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry, but we have a witness in court and these monologues are really contrary to the system --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey knows the rules. He's not doing the direct examination. And he should control his Prosecutors. He knows the correct procedure. He knows that they're tainting the witness's independent memory by doing those things and I do object, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas. I think I have already made the ruling. Ms. Issa, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, I was indicating to you that I read out to you a portion of the report, which was dated 16 July, from the command of the Bratunac Brigade that says that: "Colonel Blagojevic visited troops in the Milici Light Infantry Brigade, units of the 65th Protection Regiment, the Protection Motorised Regiment, parts of the MUP and the 5th Engineering Battalion and defined their tasks, and organised their joint action and communications." Are you aware of the troops that he visited, of these troops -- or of these trips?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, during the week after the fall of Srebrenica where was Colonel Blagojevic spending most of his time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: The week after the fall of Srebrenica you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the -- Srebrenica fell on a particular day, sir. So during that week, after that day when Srebrenica fell, where was Mr. -- where was Colonel Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Well, I've already said. I told you a moment ago where we were walking around those days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. What I'm trying to ask you, sir, was: Where was he -- where did he spend most of his time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: In the brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. When you travelled -- the times that you've told us when you travelled in the vehicle with Mr. -- with Colonel Blagojevic, was it equipped with a radio?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I don't think they had anything, no radio.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Was either yourself or Colonel Blagojevic or the driver carrying a radio, a hand-held radio or a Motorola?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, where did Colonel Blagojevic spend his evenings during that week after the fall of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Well, mostly he would go to his apartment to spend the night there. He was at the brigade during working hours, and then he would go home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I was there. I spent quite a lot of time at the reception desk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. During that same week, did you see UNPROFOR soldiers in Bratunac, DutchBat soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I saw them on one occasion. I don't remember where I saw them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. When you say you don't remember where you saw them, are you saying you saw them in Bratunac but you don't know specifically where, or elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: No. In Bratunac. Now, whether I saw them at lunch or somewhere else, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you see buses in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Which bus?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did you see buses carrying people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I saw some buses along the road. Where they were going, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were they carrying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Well, there were passengers, people. How should I know who?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they men or women?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I think there were more men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of, sir, of the execution that took place at the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware, sir, that there's evidence that Muslims were beaten and killed in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell us, sir, if Colonel Blagojevic travelled with an escort everywhere he went?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Well, not always.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether at some point he visited Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: At what point, Your Honour, are we talking about? And I would like to know what the relevance is with respect to Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We have the same question, too, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I actually withdraw that. It's really not all that important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I have no more questions, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. I think it's time for a break. Let's take a break and we'll resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas. Your cross-examination, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Karnavas:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to speak up. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, as we just heard, if you could just speak up a little bit. And it might help also if you could look towards me so we can have a nice dialogue and I can get you back home safely and soundly, perhaps as early as tomorrow. I understand it, sir, that currently you're working for SFOR. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. From the documents that I've received from the Prosecution, it shows that you're currently employed with -- as a cook -- or you were. I see. You were employed as a cook with SFOR in Camp Connor. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you work there, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I left the base a year ago, or rather, I didn't leave. I --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You lost your job?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long had you worked as a cook over there at the SFOR camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: 11 months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what sort of soldiers -- what country are those soldiers from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: America.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And currently, as I understand it, you're unemployed. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your mother is ill, as I have read in one of the documents, or was ill?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes, she's in hospital now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it as you're sitting here today, you're also a little apprehensive or you have some fear, because after all you're here at The Hague testifying in a trial where your former commander is being accused of some serious crimes. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But as you know, you're not a suspect in this case. And I'm sure the Prosecution has told you that you will be going home after testifying, so certainly there's nothing to be worried about. You understand that. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, before I talk to you about your testimony, the Prosecutor here is claiming that your commander, Colonel Blagojevic, committed murder, committed extermination, committed forcible transfer, committed or was assisting in genocide. Did you ever see Colonel Blagojevic commit any of those crimes in your presence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Prosecution also claims that Colonel Blagojevic was planning all of these events, was planning the murder, the extermination, the forcible transfer, genocide, all of that. Did you ever see him participate in any meetings where he was sitting around, planning on how to wipe off the face of the earth all these Muslims that were coming from Srebrenica? Did you ever hear that or see him planning this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Prosecution also indicates that your commander was instigating, in other words he was telling folks like you, the soldiers, the military police, Momir Nikolic, instigating them, in other words getting them -- leading them on to go ahead and commit these crimes, kill the Muslim prisoners. Did you ever see or hear your commander do any of those things?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, sir, when I read your statement and I hear your testimony, what becomes abundantly clear to me is that if anything, if anything, your commander was trying to make sure that no one under his command harmed any single prisoner. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: In my opinion, yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And I'm -- now I'm going to walk you through day-by-day, blow-by-blow, so we have a clear picture. And as I understand it that because of the passage of time - we're talking close to ten years - that you're a little bit off on the dates. Correct? You're not quite sure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But as far as you recall of what you did and where you were, you believe that your memory is fairly good. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was once commander left and Colonel Blagojevic came, then you, along with the other gentleman, Mr. Bajic [sic], I believe his name is, continued to perform those duties. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Colonel Blagojevic was there less than two months before the attack on Srebrenica occurred.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember exactly, but yes, roughly thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you gave your statement initially, the first time, to the Office of the Prosecution, you had indicated that you went to Pribicevac where the forward command post of the 3rd Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade was located on the very same day that Srebrenica fell. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes, but I corrected that later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And I'm going to talk about that. And then a couple -- two days later as I understand it, you were contacted by phone and by the Office of the Prosecution. And at that point, which was the first opportunity that you had, you informed the Office of the -- the folks from the Office of the Prosecution that having spoken to your wife, who refreshed your memory, you believed that you had actually gone to Pribicevac two or three days before the fall of Srebrenica. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So -- and as I understand it or I'm trying to understand it, it is your wife that is actually refreshing your memory, as opposed to you having an independent memory whether it was two, three, or maybe four or five or six days before the fall of Srebrenica that you had actually gone up to Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: She reminded me of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Is it possible, sir, that you might have been up there more than two or three days, four or five days or six days, because we've heard testimony here in court that from the 5th to the 11th, Colonel Blagojevic was the entire time up in Pribicevac. So could you be mistaken? Could it be more than two or three days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Possibly. I'm not quite sure how many days it was. I don't think it was more than three or four.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And it was on that particular day, the day that Srebrenica fell, which incidentally is July 11th, 1995, that you recall that your commander gave you an order to go up a hill and to have a chat with some soldiers. And you think that it was regarding food supplies or something to that nature. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there -- the commander told you to stay up there because he was planning on coming up. So there was no need for you to return, that he would be coming up, and then together you all would be going back to Pribicevac or Bratunac at some point. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after four or five hours of being there, as I understand it, you came to the conclusion that your commander in all likelihood was not going to come up. And so you took it upon yourself to get a ride back into town to Bratunac from a vehicle that was heading in that direction. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Might I ask: How long would it have taken you to go from that location to Bratunac, given the conditions of the road and what was happening on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Perhaps an hour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And do you know whether when you returned to Bratunac it was still daylight, was it late in the afternoon, was it getting dark? Do you recall the lighting conditions of the day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: It was about 5.00 or 6.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, is that because you looked at your watch and you saw that it was 5.00 or 6.00, or are you basing that on the lighting conditions of the particular -- of that day, and we're talking, you know, the middle of July or July 11th, 1995, to be precise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I saw it on the clock which was at the reception desk of the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And when you went to the brigade, did you go up to meet with Colonel Blagojevic, or did you just sit around where you normally sit waiting for your next assignment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, okay. Yes, did you go see the colonel or were you just waiting for your next assignment? Which of the two?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-210
utterances.text: I was waiting for my next assignment at the reception desk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And here is the reason why I'm asking that question: Because it is our understanding that Colonel Blagojevic does not return to the Bratunac Brigade headquarters until way later in the day, perhaps as late as 9.00 or 10.00 at night. So my question is: Is it possible, sir, that you could be wrong as far as the timing when you saw Mr. Blagojevic next?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object to the form of that question. I don't think -- Clearly, it appears to me that Mr. Karnavas is attempting to give evidence at this point. He could simply ask the

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: it's certainly objectionable for him to indicate to the witness what he thinks. He's not here to give evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll rephrase, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Please rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it possible, sir, that you might be wrong as far as seeing Colonel Blagojevic as early as 5.00 or 6.00 in the afternoon on July 11th? Could it be that it was much later at the time when at least we know that you indicated it was 10.00 or 11.00 when he went off to go to his apartment or when you last saw him?

utterances.speaker: How do you know or anything -- something to that effect.  But
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not sure, but I think this was towards the evening, perhaps around 5.00 or 6.00. And Colonel Blagojevic went to his apartment quite late, at about 10.00 or 11.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But at 5.00 or 6.00, was it -- well, let me rephrase the question. Can you sit -- as you sit here today, can you tell us with certainty that it was around 5.00 or 6.00 that you saw Colonel Blagojevic, or are you not sure, which of the two?

utterances.speaker: How do you know or anything -- something to that effect.  But
utterances.text: Perhaps I'm wrong, but it was late in the afternoon. I'm not sure about the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the following day would be the 12th of July. And as I understand your testimony, it was the following day that you were asked by Colonel Blagojevic to go to the Vuk Karadzic school. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: How do you know or anything -- something to that effect.  But
utterances.text: To stop by on my way home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But I'm trying to get a fix on the date. So if we use -- if we use the 11th, which is the fall of Srebrenica, the following day would be the 12th. Okay. So is it your testimony or is it your memory that it was on that particular day, on the evening of the 12th, that Colonel Blagojevic told you on your way home to stop at the Vuk Karadzic school?

utterances.speaker: How do you know or anything -- something to that effect.  But
utterances.text: I'm not sure about the dates and when it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. First let me just ask you: When you got there, as I understand it, the prisoners were located not in the school, not inside the classrooms on the first and the second floor, ground floor, but in the gym, which is next to the school. Correct?

utterances.speaker: How do you know or anything -- something to that effect.  But
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the numbers of prisoners were -- could fit into that gymnasium. Correct?

utterances.speaker: How do you know or anything -- something to that effect.  But
utterances.text: I didn't see how many were there. I could just hear them talking, but I don't know what they were saying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But as far as you remember, there were no prisoners in the school on that particular day, on that particular evening, when you went there?

utterances.speaker: How do you know or anything -- something to that effect.  But
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, before going to that school, I want to -- let's go back a little bit. You indicated that at some point you overheard a conversation - this is what you told the Prosecutor when you were interviewed - you overheard a conversation where the commander was instructing, ordering, Nikolic to keep everything in order and not to behave brutally toward the prisoners. Do you recall first telling that to the Office of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: How do you know or anything -- something to that effect.  But
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall, as you sit here today, overhearing that conversation where the commander is telling Nikolic to keep everything in order and not to behave brutally toward the prisoners? Do you recall hearing that?

utterances.speaker: How do you know or anything -- something to that effect.  But
utterances.text: Yes. This was in front of the brigade, near the reception desk, as the commander was going home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then -- well, just let me ask you this: Did Nikolic by any chance say: "Well, you know, I have instructions from Kosoric and Popovic that we're going to kill these prisoners, so why not have a little fun? Why not abuse them a little bit?" Did you hear Nikolic say anything to that effect?

utterances.speaker: How do you know or anything -- something to that effect.  But
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear Nikolic tell him that he had orders from above as to what would happen to these prisoners, that they were going to be killed?

utterances.speaker: How do you know or anything -- something to that effect.  But
utterances.text: They were talking. They were saying whatever they were saying. But what he said later, I didn't really didn't hear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But nonetheless what you remember is that your commander was ordering Nikolic not to harm the prisoners. Correct?

utterances.speaker: How do you know or anything -- something to that effect.  But
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then he asked you on your way home to go and speak with the military police that were located there. Correct?

utterances.speaker: How do you know or anything -- something to that effect.  But
utterances.text: Just to go and see whether everything was all right there and to report on that, in order to avoid any incidents from occurring, to make sure that everything is as it should be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But in your statement, in your statement, you also indicate - and I'm going to read from it - it says here: "He further told he that I should tell the guards posted there that they should not cause any problems." Correct?

utterances.speaker: How do you know or anything -- something to that effect.  But
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, if I understand what you're telling us, that your commander first wanted you to go there to make sure that the prisoners were not being mistreated. Correct?

utterances.speaker: How do you know or anything -- something to that effect.  But
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And secondly, he was also telling you to give an order to his -- to those guards, the military police, to make sure that they did not harm any of the prisoners. Correct?

utterances.speaker: How do you know or anything -- something to that effect.  But
utterances.text: I was just conveying Colonel Blagojevic's message. I could not issue any orders to anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that you were not issuing the order. The order had been issued by the commander. And so you were conveying the commander's order, were you not?

utterances.speaker: How do you know or anything -- something to that effect.  But
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in fact, I take it that you understood at that particular point in time the importance of your commander's order, did you not?

utterances.speaker: How do you know or anything -- something to that effect.  But
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in fact because you understood and you appreciated exactly what your commander was trying to do, you, when you went to the Vuk Karadzic school, you conveyed the orders personally to the guards. Correct?

utterances.speaker: How do you know or anything -- something to that effect.  But
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in conveying those orders, you also had an opportunity to sit there, look around, and to see whether any atrocities were occurring, did you not?

utterances.speaker: How do you know or anything -- something to that effect.  But
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you saw none, did you?

utterances.speaker: How do you know or anything -- something to that effect.  But
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But nonetheless, nonetheless, you instructed the military police, the guards over there, you instructed them or you passed along the order that had been given to you by Colonel Blagojevic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: How do you know or anything -- something to that effect.  But
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your commander had told you that in the event, in the event, you saw something that was improper, that you were to come back to him, locate him, find him, and inform him. Correct?

utterances.speaker: How do you know or anything -- something to that effect.  But
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you saw nothing improper. Correct?

utterances.speaker: How do you know or anything -- something to that effect.  But
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And not seeing anything improper, you then went home?

utterances.speaker: How do you know or anything -- something to that effect.  But
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the next day sometime around 7.00, you had an opportunity to see your commander. Correct?

utterances.speaker: How do you know or anything -- something to that effect.  But
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your commander asked you what, if anything, unusual you had seen the night before when you went to visit the guards that were guarding the prisoners at the gymnasium of the Vuk Karadzic school. Correct?

utterances.speaker: How do you know or anything -- something to that effect.  But
utterances.text: Yes. He asked me whether everything was all right, and I said that it was. And he said, Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I take it the colonel, your commander, must have believed you. Correct?

utterances.speaker: How do you know or anything -- something to that effect.  But
utterances.text: I don't know. I just conveyed what I saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well he must have trusted you to pass on -- to go and check up on the prisoners, did he not?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not understand what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
